subject: SilverOak private K8s roadmap: network posture, node roles, and persistent data approach
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Lopez <andrew.lopez@silveroakhealth.com>, SilverOak Infrastructure <infra@silveroakhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SilverOak private K8s roadmap: network posture, node roles, and persistent data approach

Hi Andrew / infra team —

Thanks for the intake doc and the site inventory attached (thank you for the detail). I wanted to capture the high- level architecture decisions we'll need sign-off on before we lock the SOW: networking model, node role decomposition, and the persistent data strategy for model artifacts and KV caching. This note is a concise proposal and a short list of action items so we can align next week on the on-site window.

Proposal (short):
- Network: single VPC with dedicated private VLANs per rack; east-west routed at TOR using BGP learned routes to the cluster CNI. Primary CNI: Calico in BGP mode for policy enforcement + native BGP peering to TORs.
- Node roles: control-plane (3x reserved masters), compute-gpu (N GPUs per node, mixed T4/ A100 depending on rack), storage-workers (SSD-backed with 8x NVMe local for ephemeral cache).
- Storage: durable block via Rook/Ceph for long-lived PVs (model artifacts, DBs), local NVMe for ephemeral model cache (mounted as local PersistentVolume), and a CSI snapshot+backup policy to replicate critical PVs to S3-compatible on-prem gateway nightly.

Open questions we need to decide on by kickoff:
1) MTU and overlay choice — we recommend MTU 9000 where possible and Calico BGP (no VXLAN) to avoid overlay overhead for KV-heavy workloads. If you have cross-rack VXLAN constraints we can fall back to IP-in-IP.
2) Encryption at rest — do you require HSM/KMS integration (we support customer KMS via AWS KMS proxy or on-prem HashiCorp Vault HSM)?
3) Backup retention — default proposal is 30 days daily snapshots, weekly 90-day rollups for model artifacts.
4) Service account mapping and AD/LDAP integration for kube API access (we'll use OIDC for short-lived tokens unless you prefer AD service accounts).

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (draft SOW), silveroak-ops-inventory.xlsx (site inventory)

Next steps: please confirm which of the three storage/backup constraints above are mandatory for sign-off and whether you want us to include Portworx/Longhorn as an alternative to Rook in the SOW. Happy to run a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the choices.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: SilverOak private K8s roadmap: network posture, node roles, and persistent data approach

Naomi —

Appreciate the concise set of choices. A few clarifications from our side so we can sign quickly: 
- Encryption: we must use our on-prem KMS (Thales) for anything holding PHI. I'll need a short integration note to share with our security reviewer.
- NVMe for cache: yes, we'd like local NVMe per compute node for the inference KV cache. Latency is critical for real-time scoring.
- MTU: our switches support jumbo frames but the SAN/backup path currently uses MTU 1500. Is Calico BGP still safe in a mixed-MTU environment?
- Backup window: we prefer backups to be outside our 02:00–05:00 job window; nightly after 05:30 is fine.

Also can you confirm the recommended storage class names and CSI drivers you expect us to have available? That will help our infra team confirm package installs prior to the on-site.

—Andrew
Andrew Lopez
Head of Infrastructure, SilverOak Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Lopez <andrew.lopez@silveroakhealth.com>
Cc: SilverOak Infrastructure <infra@silveroakhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SilverOak private K8s roadmap: network posture, node roles, and persistent data approach

Thanks Andrew — good questions. Short answers inline: 
- On-prem KMS: yes, we can integrate with Thales/HSM for envelope encryption. We'll include an appendix on the KMS integration steps and the roles/keys we need.
- NVMe local cache: we'll configure a local PV class (storageclass: local-nvme, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer) and mount it to a node-affinity pod (model-cache). We'll propose a 4–8 GiB per model-slot baseline and can size up based on perf testing.
- Mixed MTU: Calico in BGP non-overlay mode will operate fine with mixed MTU across different leafs, but you should avoid MTU blackholes. We'll add MTU validation tests in the preflight checklist; if cross-rack MTU is inconsistent we'll shift to IP-in-IP on affected racks.
- Storage classes and CSI: primary durable: rook-ceph-block (provisioner: rook-ceph.csi.ceph.com). Backup/replication: restic/s3 gateway or Velero against on-prem S3 compatible gateway (we'll run the backup agent in a control namespace). Ephemeral/local cache: local-nvme provisioner (compliant with CSI local-volume).

I'll ask Karthik to put together the preflight checklist (network tests, MTU checks, KMS handshake, node labeling matrix) and Marissa will publish a delivery timeline.

Can you confirm the on-site network contact and an initial 2-hour window next Tuesday?

Naomi

Subject: Re: SilverOak private K8s roadmap: network posture, node roles, and persistent data approach

Andrew / team —

I pulled together the preflight checklist below and a few concrete recommendations for the SOW. I'm attaching the checklist excerpt inline for quick review.

Preflight checklist (short):
- Network
  * Verify MTU across TORs and storage fabric (run iperf3 + ping to check fragmentation). Goal: 9000 where possible, fallback safe to 1500.
  * Confirm BGP session on TORs and provide ASNs/peer IPs to us prior to on-site.
  * Egress: identify allowed outbound CIDRs, firewall rules for model telemetry (Datadog), and S3-gateway endpoints for backup.
- Nodes
  * Control plane: 3x VMs/hosts with 32GB RAM, 4 CPUs reserved min, etc.
  * Compute GPU: label topology.kubernetes.io/zone and node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu. We support mixed node-pools; recommend homogeneous GPU families per pool.
  * Storage nodes: ensure NVMe health tests (smartctl) and required local-ssd firmware up-to-date.
- Storage/Backup
  * Rook/Ceph cluster: 3 OSD nodes minimum for durability; SSD-backed OSDs for model artifacts.
  * Local cache: local-nvme storageclass for ephemeral model KV caches.
  * Snapshot policy: daily snapshots at 05:30 (outside your job window), 30-day retention. Weekly rollup to 90 days for model artifacts.

SOW recommendations (summary):
- Include a KMS appendix for Thales integration and an ops checklist requiring the infra team to provide credentials in a secure vault prior to the on-site.
- We'll deliver a 2-stage rollout: verification cluster (3-node non-prod) for validation -> pilot with 2 racks -> production cutover.
- Run a preflight day for MTU/BGP tests and a follow-up day for storage/OSD validation.

If this looks good I will fold these bullets into the SOW. Also note: if you prefer Portworx we can swap the storage section — Portworx gives more predictable QoS for multi-tenant block stores but requires a license.

Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for confirming the KMS constraint and the NVMe requirement. From delivery/logistics: we can hold the preflight on 2027-04-20 (MTU/BGP/day 1) and the storage validation on 2027-04-21. Can you confirm the on-site network owner and their mobile number so our field engineer can coordinate arrival?

Action items for SilverOak prior to preflight:
- Provide TOR BGP peer details (ASN, peer IPs) and allow SSH to a switch for our netops engineer for 2 hours during the preflight.
- Confirm credentials for Thales KMS integration in your secure vault (we only need a service account and wrapping key details).
- Pre-install package list for the validation cluster: kubeadm, docker/containerd, ceph-common, ceph-csi, calicoctl. I'll attach a one-page ops quickstart to the SOW.

I'll update the draft SOW with the schedule and circulate for signature once we receive the above.

Marissa Cole
